Covers the town's general fund. Water, sewer and other enterprise funds and independent authorities are separate.
Left out: transfers in ($55,448) and out ($11,470,410) between the town's own funds and other financing sources such as borrowing, which are not new revenue or spending.

Employee benefits the town records under general government ($4,153,496, such as health insurance and pensions for town staff) are spread across the town's own departments in proportion to their size, as in other states. Schools and debt service are left out of that spread.
The state reports revenue only as property tax, state, federal and all other, so fees, fines and local charges are not shown separately.

Political money counts contributions from PACs, unions, businesses (program-book ads), registered lobbyists and state contractors to Town of Windsor's party town committees, filed with the State Elections Enforcement Commission since 2023. Other individual donors ($85,805 in the same period) and party and candidate committees are not counted. Candidates for town office file with the town clerk, so their own committees are not included, and town committees also support state candidates.
